title: Concordium Analytics - Success Liftoff Sync
summary: Kickoff for implementation and runtime handoff. Discussed staging plan, VPC networking, SSO/KMS requirements, target latency SLOs, and pilot dataset. Agreed next steps: share runbook, security pack, and schedule bench repro for dedicated pool sizing.
action_items: Diego Alvarez: Share implementation runbook + onboarding checklist (due 2026-03-04)
Priya Narang: Run baseline throughput/latency perf test with Concordium sample workload and send results (due 2026-03-08)
Lena Park: Provide sample ingress patterns and expected token distribution for 3 workloads (due 2026-03-03)
Tom Baird: Confirm SOC 2 requirement list and KMS vendor details (due 2026-03-05)
next_steps: Set up staging VPC access and service account (Concordium infra)
transcript:
Meeting header: Mar 1 2026 15:00 PT, Duration 48m, Attendees: Maya, Diego, Priya (Redwood) - Evan, Lena, Tom (Concordium)

[00:00] Maya Chen: All right, hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. We have Diego and Priya with me; can each of you confirm you're on?
[00:06] Diego Alvarez: Yep, Diego here, CSM.
[00:08] Priya Narang: Priya, SE. Hey folks.
[00:10] Evan Ross: Evan Ross, Head of ML at Concordium. Good to be here.
[00:12] Lena Park: Lena, Platform team.
[00:13] Tom Baird: Tom Baird, Security.

[00:30] Maya Chen: Cool. Agenda — quick goals: align on pilot scope, timeline to staging, network and security checkpoints, and the runtime sizing bench so we can recommend Dedicated sizing. Anything to add?
[00:40] Evan: Sounds good. High level we want to validate cost/latency tradeoffs on the two main paths: low-latency customer-facing API and cheaper batch embeddings.
[00:47] Priya: Great, we'll focus tests for both. Quick note: our runtime supports prefix KV caching and continuous batching which will bump throughput for batch jobs; we'll show config suggestions.

[01:12] Lena: On networking — Concordium can't allow public egress from staging. We need VPC peering or private interconnect. Also, our firewall team requires static egress IPs.
[01:22] Maya: Understood. For Redwood Private we can support customer-managed networking with VPC endpoints; for Hosted we have NAT ranges but I know static IPs are more complicated. Diego, can you drop the network diagram?
[01:30] Diego: Yep, I'll include a template VPC peering diagram; I'll also flag the static IP options and the Dedicated pool approach which can live in your VPC (private deploy).

[02:05] Tom: Also, KMS — we need to hold keys on our KMS (Hashi / AWS KMS). Are we able to integrate? Full key custody?
[02:13] Priya: We support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integration in Private deployments. For Hosted we can offer envelope encryption but customer HSM-only is a Private option. There's some nuance with token-level logging — Diego will follow-up with the exact audit log masking patterns.
[02:34] Tom: Okay please call that out. Our auditors will ask for key scoping and rotation cadence.

[03:00] Evan: On success criteria for pilot: 1) 95th percentile latency under 200ms for customer API at p50 workload; 2) Embed batch cost under $X per million tokens (we discussed target in email); 3) No PII stored in logs — retention 30 days.
[03:14] Maya: That maps nicely. We'll mark those as acceptance criteria for the pilot. Priya — can you run that perf test and include 95p?
[03:20] Priya: Yes, we'll run p50/p95 and show token-level cost breakdowns in the perf report. We'll also demo the Optimize suggestions for quantization and batching.

[04:05] Evan: Quick question around rollouts — we have an internal canary strategy. If we use Redwood Dedicated, can we do canary traffic split between two model versions without double cost?
[04:16] Priya: You can split by route with traffic shaping. There will be double inference for mirrored traffic if both are active. You can leverage fallback policies to only route a percentage to the new variant; caching helps mitigate cost for repeated prefixes. Also we support canary by weight without duplicating for every request via warm KV caches for the primary.
[04:39] Evan: Okay noted. We need to understand economics of that.

[05:05] Lena: How do we get observability? Specifically, token-level cost, per-model latency, and tracing to our Datadog instance.
[05:12] Diego: Redwood Console exports per-route and per-model telemetry. We have a Datadog integration, and you can pull traces via our tracing hooks. We'll send the dashboard templates (link: https://redwood.internal/templates/observability).
[05:30] Lena: I've added that link to our internal ticket.

[06:00] Tom: Any SOC 2/ISO docs we can pre-share? Also, SSO — we want SAML with SCIM and RBAC roles mapped to our groups.
[06:10] Maya: Yes, we have a security pack. We'll share SOC2 report and ISO attestations plus the SAML/SCIM setup guide. We support SCIM provisioning and roles mapping. Diego will attach the SSO playbook.
[06:28] Tom: Good. Also, audit logs — we must show redactions for PII. Does Redwood provide redaction rules?
[06:34] Priya: We have configurable log redaction and can mask token text. For Private deployments you can enforce stricter retention. We'll document default retention and masking examples.

[07:10] Evan: For the sample data for perf — we'll provide three workloads: customer-chat (short prompt, low tokens), support-ticket summarization (mid length), and nightly embedding batch (longer sequences).
[07:20] Priya: Perfect. Please include token distribution and typical sequence lengths so we pick kernel paths and batching strategy. That matters for the runtime kernels and quantization choices.

[08:05] Evan: One more — we talked about quantization earlier. If we quantize model weights on Dedicated, does that affect output quality? We need to measure regression.
[08:15] Priya: Yes, quantization trades off numeric fidelity vs speed/cost. Our Optimize toolkit recommends a quant profile and runs evals against your prompt set to estimate regressions. We'll include quality thresholds. We'll also show A/B eval harness so you can spot regressions.

[09:00] Maya: OK timeline proposal: Week 1 (this week) — share runbook, security pack and staging access steps. Week 2 — Concordium provides sample traffic + staging infra. Week 3 — Redwood runs perf bench and shares results. Week 4 — recommendation for Dedicated sizing and pilot sign-off. Is that realistic?
[09:19] Evan: Tight but doable. We might need an extra buffer for security review.
[09:24] Tom: Our security review usually takes ~10 business days but we can parallelize with perf runs if you don't need keys until later.

[10:00] Diego: We'll make sure the runbook separates "network & access" from "KMS & keys" so you can start perf runs without granting key custody.

[12:45] Lena: Small nit — do you support connector to our internal feature store for context retrieval? We want to call the model with external context pulled on the customer side, not sent to Redwood.
[12:55] Priya: Yes, you can do local retrieval and pass only the minimal prompt to Redwood; many customers do that to keep PII inside their VPC. We'll add integration notes for retrieval + minimal prefix caching.

[15:00] Evan: On capacity — what happens if we exceed Dedicated pool? Do you have overflow to hosted?
[15:07] Priya: We support smart routing policies: you can set fallback to a compatible hosted variant. There are config options for cost-first and latency-first fallback. We'll show defaults.
[15:20] Maya: We'll also call out SLA impacts if fallback kicks in.

[18:40] Tom: Compliance question — are audit logs exportable to our SIEM? We need that for e-discovery.
[18:46] Diego: Yes, logs are exportable; retained copies can be delivered to your S3 bucket or forwarded to your SIEM with masking. We'll include the export runbook.

[22:10] Evan: For the perf bench — can you run both GPU and CPU variants? We mostly expect to use GPU but want to know the delta.
[22:18] Priya: We'll run GPU-optimized profiles; CPU inference is available but not recommended for production for your scale. We'll include comparative numbers.

[28:00] Evan: Side question — we previously evaluated "AnthrAI" — their docs flagged some issues around long-tail latency. How do you handle tail-latency?
[28:10] Priya: Our runtime has continuous batching and attention optimizations plus active KV cache invalidation policies. We also support warm-keep instances to reduce cold-starts. We'll document tail-latency mitigations.

[34:00] Lena: About ticketing — who owns post-pilot runbook updates?
[34:06] Diego: Diego will be the primary CSM point; after pilot we handoff to Success Ops for ongoing runbook updates. We'll align on a cadence.

[38:30] Maya: Let me recap: Diego sends runbook, security artifacts, SSO guide; Priya runs perf and posts results; Concordium provides sample workload and infra access. Follow-up call 03-10 to review perf and security checklist. Any corrections?
[38:48] Evan: That's right. Add Tom's auditor checklist to the security pack.
[38:52] Tom: I'll DM a list of must-haves — key rotation, retention windows, and audit export.

[43:00] Maya: Great. Thanks everyone — we'll wrap. Diego will email artifacts by EOD tomorrow.
[43:08] Diego: Yep, will do.
[43:10] Priya: Thanks, bye.
[43:12] Evan: Thanks all. Bye.

Notes: Transcript has occasional mis-heard words (e.g., AnthrAI transcribed as Anthr_R). Shared artifacts referenced: runbook (link in email), security pack (drive link placeholder), observability templates.

End of transcript.
